overview: White grabs space on the kingside with g4-g5, Bg2 on the long diagonal and h4-h5 to follow, ignoring the centre. Black answers 2...c6 and simply builds the d5/c6 centre and develops, usually with ...Bf5 or ...Bg4 and ...e6, aiming to punish the loosened kingside.

white_ideas.idea: g4-g5 gains space and kicks the f6 square
Bg2 on the long diagonal against b7 and d5
h4-h5 pawn advance to attack on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5/c6 and ...e5 later
Develop the bishop outside the pawn chain with ...Bf5 or ...Bg4
Hit the advanced g5 pawn with ...h6 or ...Qd7

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on g5 and h-file with a fianchettoed bishop against a Black d5/c6 centre

character.notes: White pushes flank pawns early and leaves his own king exposed; Black has a clear central game. Unbalanced and risky for White.

gambit.notes: No material is given on purpose in the main line.

soundness.notes: The Grob is generally considered dubious; Black simply develops and gets a comfortable centre.

structure.notes: Black holds d5/c6 against a white flank advance; the centre is undecided.

approach.notes: Played for surprise; strong players almost never choose it.

level.notes: Few moves to learn but an unsound idea; not a first repertoire choice.

character.reason: Flank pawn pushes leave White exposed and the game becomes unbalanced and risky.

gambit.reason: No pawn is on offer after 2...c6; g5 simply advances.

soundness.reason: The Grob is regarded as unsound; Black gets a free centre.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided while White plays on the flank.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Grob.

level.reason: Dubious lines are never Beginner and nothing here is deep.

plans.reason: Flank pawns advance with Bg2 on the long diagonal.
